article_title: CoreWeave Launches Forge, Brings Vera Rubin NVL72 Online and Says It Will Offer Vera CPU Racks for Agent Sandboxes

content_preview.title: CoreWeave Launches Forge, Brings Vera Rubin NVL72 Online and Says It Will Offer Vera CPU Racks for Agent Sandboxes
content_preview.summary: At its Fully Connected event, CoreWeave announced Vera Rubin NVL72 availability, plans to offer NVIDIA Vera CPUs, and the Forge platform for training and agent improvement.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

CoreWeave used its Fully Connected event to announce three infrastructure moves. According to [NVIDIA's blog](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/coreweave-agentic-ai-vera-rubin/), published September 30, 2026, the cloud provider announced availability of NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems with Spectrum-X 102.4T Ethernet networking, said it will also offer the NVIDIA Vera CPU, and launched CoreWeave Forge, "a connected environment for training, evaluating and improving models and agents on N...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well structured News piece (700 words, inside the 400-1200 range) with Overview, What We Know, What We Don't Know and Analysis sections. Technical detail is accurate and appropriately hedged. Does not conflate CoreWeave Forge with any other product named Forge; Forge is described only via the NVIDIA post and the SiliconANGLE quote.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both snapshots from disk via gunzip (source-0.html.gz = NVIDIA blog 'From Training to Production, NVIDIA and CoreWeave Close the Loop on Agentic AI', Sept 30 2026, by Stuart Pitts, HTTP 200; source-1.html.gz = SiliconANGLE keynote analysis by Chad Wilson, updated Sept 30 2026, HTTP 200). Both snapshots contain the full cited text (not stubs). Source-0 confirms: availability of Vera Rubin NVL72 with Spectrum-X 102.4T Ethernet; Cognition first customer running production workloads; 4.8x total token throughput for SWE-2 inference over GB200 NVL72 (Cognition's own early tests, workload from sampled FrontierCode tasks); production cluster stood up in days; thousands of GPUs in nine months; operated via CKS, SUNK, Mission Control, Sandboxes, Inference; 128 CPUs / 11,264 cores per rack / more than 11,000 concurrent environments at one core each; more than 3x faster sandbox startup and 1.7x Terminal-Bench gain (both CoreWeave testing); Forge unifies Weights & Biases, OpenPipe expertise and marimo; ARIA GA; Agent Lens new, 20% better failure detection and half the cost; Sandboxes GA; Serverless RL 1.4x faster at 40% lower cost; Dynamo powers managed inference and RL Rollouts (private preview); Canva, Capital One, MasterClass among first on Forge; event in San Francisco. The direct quote 'a connected environment for training, evaluating and improving models and agents on NVIDIA accelerated computing' and the fragment 'has historically been split across tools from different vendors' are verbatim. Source-1 confirms the Vellante quote 'What you're seeing CoreWeave do strategically is they're expanding out beyond compute.' verbatim, his title (chief analyst, theCUBE Research), the Forge mention, and the paid-media-partner disclosure. Manifest suspicious_patterns is null for both sources; nothing to override. Both domains (blogs.nvidia.com line 363, siliconangle.com line 381) are on config/source_allowlist.txt. Nothing in the article rests on the excluded CoreWeave investor press release.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All figures trace to the NVIDIA post and are attributed in the body to NVIDIA, Cognition or CoreWeave's own testing; the 4.8x figure keeps the 'up to' qualifier, the hardware baseline (GB200 NVL72), the workload (SWE-2) and who measured it (Cognition). The What We Don't Know section states that none of the figures are independently verified and that no availability date or pricing is given; none is invented. Available-now vs planned is kept distinct: Vera Rubin NVL72 'announced availability' and Forge launched (with ARIA and Sandboxes GA, RL Rollouts private preview) versus Vera CPU 'will also offer' / 'planned deployment', matching the title's 'Says It Will Offer'. The earlier-coverage link /article/2026-05/21-nvidia-hand-delivers-first-vera-cpus-to-anthropic-openai-and-spacexai-as-agentic-ai-drives-a-new-cpu-moment resolves to an existing published article. Minor gaps: the NVIDIA post says Vera Rubin is available to 'early-access customers' and that CoreWeave received its first production racks 'earlier this month'; the article omits the early-access qualifier, so 'brings online' should be read as early-access availability, not general availability. The post also gives no baseline for the 3x sandbox-startup, 1.7x Terminal-Bench, 20% and half-cost claims; the article repeats them as attributed claims without a baseline but does not overstate them.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. Vendor claims are attributed rather than adopted. The Analysis section is short, hedged and framed as NVIDIA's own framing.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Machine Herald article covers CoreWeave's Fully Connected announcements or Forge. The only related item is the May 2026 Vera CPU delivery article, correctly cross-referenced as background. New topic.
concerns: Vera Rubin availability is early-access per the NVIDIA post; the article and title do not say so explicitly, though they do not claim general availability.

NVIDIA, the author of the primary source, is also CoreWeave's long-time technology partner; the article attributes all numbers to NVIDIA but does not state the commercial relationship (the cited sources do not describe an investment, so it was not asserted).
Baselines are unstated in the source for the 3x, 1.7x, 20% and half-cost figures.
recommendations: In future coverage, state 'early-access' when the source does and name the vendor relationship when the sole primary source is a partner's blog.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-attributed and appropriately hedged. Every claim verified against the snapshots; no fabricated specifics; availability versus plans are distinguished. The early-access omission is a nuance, not an error, and does not warrant a corrections record.
